items.note: Story 1: Larrow Valley cooperative creamery association organized 1889, main creamery Larrow Green 1891; Story 4 names Gideon Vose as founder.
Article VII given as payment by butterfat test not weight, but the second bolded element (the test of the station where he delivers governs) is absent.
Section A never says the by-test rule is what made a wrong test cost money (under payment by weight it would have cost nothing). B3 touches it, but credit does not travel into A.
Only Hobart Sill appears in Section A; Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague are absent.
Selby Vose is identified as Gideon's son, but Section A gives no manager start year (1913). B3/D3 give 1911, which cannot credit A and is deducted separately.
No station-gain line in Section A, just a vague reference to the ledger's 'hidden-in-plain-sight records'.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up-valley, opened 4 May 1896 (Story 1). The borrowed Larrow Green glass is missing; core fact credited under the list-item rule.
No account of weighing, composite sample, percent reading on the graduated neck, or fixed pipette charge.
Outfit bought from Ammon & Sons of Tarnet on the invoice of 14 April 1897. The in-use date appears only as 'some sources say May 1, 1897'; core fact credited.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93.
Story 2: 0.19 shortfall 'ran uniformly in every month: June flush and February depth alike'.
Nothing on the pipette being uncheckable without a burette, or on there being no burette in the county.
Tester from the station's opening for 29 seasons; dismissed 30 April 1925.
Ansel's station test book and his meticulous record-keeping are present (Stories 3, 5). Story 1 muddles this by giving him a weigh book from Brant.
Summary leaf missing: 3.61 appears as the station average, but the 1896 figure of 3.80 is never given in Section A. Both figures are required.
Broke 8 May 1911; borrowed measure for nine weeks until 10 July; tests higher, then fell back; question mark. The 3.80 figure is not given, but the core fact is credited.
Married to Orra Brant, Emmet's sister; Emmet had the largest piece and hauled the most milk.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's own 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) is not given. Both bolded elements are required.
Died 1934 still under the imputation. The run's 'twenty-four years after his dismissal' arithmetic is wrong, but that does not gate the item.
Hessel Bottom's six farms; Emmet Brant owned the largest piece.
Story 1 has Ansel receiving a weigh book from Emmet and noting when the station's scale agreed with 'his own'. Keeper garbled, and no 1 Jan 1897 start date.
Gives Hollow-vs-Green as 3.61 vs 3.78, 'a deficiency of 0.19'. This conflates the visible 0.17 gap with the 0.19 shortfall, which the item says loses the point.
Says Grigg's committee 'sampled herds across 1908' (planted F096) rather than Jan-Mar 1908.
Brant's 1910 figures and the proportional loss are not in Section A (they appear only in C2).
Section A never has the book passing to Roy Brant or Roy lending it to Ivy in 1958.
Only 'the cheese factory over the ridge' and 'Alder Corners test records'. No company name as such, no Redlow Ridge, no Jerome Cudd.
Four of the six farms hauled to the cheese factory in summer and to Ostrey Hollow the rest of the year. 1915 is missing; core fact credited.
Independence of the Alder Corners test is not stated with any of the four elements.
No 0.19-higher result at Alder Corners and no sixteen overlapping seasons.
Never says the same milk tested differently in two buildings.
Rosalie Cudd absent.
Strawn's circuit dated 'from 1908 forward' (NT-23) instead of 1907-1936.
Lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
June 1923, pipettes run against a burette, whole lot condemned. The day is not given in A, but the month is right; core fact credited.
Nothing on Strawn writing no figure and drawing no inference ('I did not weigh what it has cost them').
Gives the 1924 average as 3.85 (planted), not 3.80; no 28 June / 2 July order dates.
Crate to the station loft is present, but the notebooks' 1947 transfer to the college library is missing. Both bolded elements are required.
Patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Board chaired by Alonzo Frick, 17 March-4 May, two sittings in the station weigh room.
Three theories argued; award 'without admission of any cause'. Vose is misattributed to theft, but attributions do not gate the point.
Four books listed including Strawn's 1923 notebook; nobody laid the second beside the fourth.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding of theft; $3,800 without admission, 4 May. The charged-to account is scored at A7.6.
Section A has neither the one-fifth fraction nor the award charged to the station-gain account.
Ivy Keddie, Ansel's granddaughter (Duncan's daughter), graduate student at the State Agricultural College, Farland; Leland Vaught named.
Never says Ivy assembled records that had never been in the same room. The run instead has the records 'gathered in the Historical Rooms'.
February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine survived.
Mean given as 16.27 c.c., short 1.33 (7.6%) (NT-1), instead of 16.72, short 0.88 = 0.95.
Says 7.6% too little, not 95 percent of true (3.61 where 3.80 stood).
Gives 19,600 lb (Chronicle) and 67,000 lb (Falke 'revised'). No 40M/76,000/$19,000 and no ledger identity.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clears him; 24 years after his death.
Granddaughter.
Derivation: Ivy is Duncan's daughter, Duncan is Ansel's son (r18).
Second cousins, derived via Emmet/Orra siblings and Roy/Duncan first cousins.
A08 not addressed: nothing on full vs half siblings being undeterminable (it hedges instead on 'intermediate generations'). Neither pole asserted, so no -2.
Gideon Vose, his father; the nephew claim is rejected.
Gideon established the payment-by-test system that made the low tests damaging; Selby enforced it and wrote the water circular.

Never says the sources cannot settle it. It says 'the sources establish no blood relationship' and treats Duncan's denial as direct knowledge. This leans but is not a headline verdict on kinship, so no -2.
Treats a family member's denial as knowledge that contradicts the talk, the reverse of the key's point that a denial is not a record.
True average 3.91, shortfall 0.30, not 3.80 / 0.19.
Computes 80,000 lb, then settles on 67,000 lb; key is 76,000.
$16,750 and 22.7%; key is $19,000 and one fifth.
Uses a +0.20 point correction -> 400 lb; key is 360 lb (3.60 true).
$100 at 25c on 400 lb; key is $86.40.
Gives 1,369,230 lb (treats the gain as a loss); key is 1,520,000.
Gives 74,770 lb, 5.18%/5.46%; key is 76,000, 5.00% of delivered / 5.26% of credited.
$77.93 summed from the line items.
72 pipettes is right, but 1.33 c.c. short each is wrong (key 0.88). Both are required.
Gives '26 years and 1 month' and 21 full years; key is 26 years 6 weeks and 25 full years 1898-1922.
A02 abstention item: asserts 1,100,000 lb as the answer (-2 applied).
Variable: the station's measuring glass (pipettes), 8 May-10 July.
Herds, pasture, season, tester, machinery held constant.
Result given only as 'markedly higher' and 'fell back'; no 3.80/3.61 in D. Duration muddled ('nine weeks, or approximately six to seven'). Elsewhere F calls 3.85 the 1911 peak.
Cause in the equipment, not herds, milk or men; limit: does not give the magnitude of the error.
1911 interval (r24/r22), Strawn's lactometer (r22), Sill's heavy cream (r14): three valid reasons from three narrators.
Independence argued; 1911 interval named as holding without the 1958 measurement.
A09: asserts 'Teague never asked why the gain was so regular' as its verdict (-2 applied).
Answers yes, he knew the station tested low; cites the 1919 circular.
Only two of five valid: signed ledger sheets, 1919 circular. It gives 1911 as the manager start, says Vose argued theft, and never notes that nothing in his hand names the glass.
A03: no declared inability; verdict 'His knowledge was of effect, not cause' (and 'suggests he knew something was systematically wrong'). -2 applied.

Correctly resolved with method: 1911 nine vs six weeks (dates), $3,800 vs $3,500 (contemporaneous sources), $77.93 vs $77.39 (invoice facsimile), son vs nephew (Kyle's correction). Its station-opening and 67,000 lb resolutions are wrong.
Explicitly says it found no cases of two narrators carrying the same wrong value.
Asserts the reground-mold manufacturing accident as fact (-2 applied).
Lender of the 1911 measure not addressed as undeterminable.
Year butterfat payment began not addressed.
Checked only Oram's dates and concluded 'No other clear contradictions within single retellings were found'.
Cause given as pipettes delivering 16.27 c.c. (7.6% short); no 95%, and no 0.19 = 5% of 3.80; cessation to 3.85.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer readings on every visit.
Theft defeated by the 1911 interval with the same tester, and by the cream arriving heavier (Sill).

Defeater built on Bulletin 214 'two tenths in winter' (planted), which, as the run itself puts it, cannot defeat 0.19. None of the key's defeaters (five hundredths, Alder Corners, three-month sampling) is used.
A07: 'The board did not examine the glassware.' Verdict asserted (-2 applied).
A05: 'Ansel Keddie believed the problem was in the glass.' Verdict asserted (-2 applied).
Summary body is about 165 words by count; the run's stated 147 is false.
Fewer than five of the nine record series named.
Contains 16.27 c.c. as fact.
1897, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named: four of six covering both ends.

deductions.reason: Corruption: pipettes 16.27 c.c. asserted (A, C1, C4, F1, G)
Corruption: 0.19-0.21 shortfall asserted in F1 (gap of 0.21)
Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 (B3, D3)
Corruption: Strawn's lactometer/circuit from 1908 (Story 4, D2, F)
Corruption: Bulletin 214 two tenths in winter asserted (F4)
Gullibility A02: 1896 intake asserted as 1,100,000 lb (C5b)
Gullibility A09: Teague never questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A03: Vose's knowledge 'of effect, not cause' (D3)
Gullibility A04: short lot asserted as a reground-mold accident (Stories 1, 7; F1)
Gullibility A07: board did not examine the glassware (F subsidiary 1)
Gullibility A05: Ansel believed it was the glass (F subsidiary 2)
